confidence_notes: I based the food and drink figures on aggregated, crowd-sourced cost-of-living sites (Expat Exchange, Traveltables, MyLifeElsewhere). Some of their data is old, for example Traveltables was last updated in 2023. Those sites put a cheap meal at about US$15, a mid-range meal for two at US$79–80, a cappuccino at US$3.50–4.90 and a domestic beer at US$2.50–3.50. I raised these figures to allow for inflation up to July 2026 and for prices at tourist-facing restaurants and bars, since an in-restaurant serving of Banks beer usually costs more than the crowd-sourced figure. I did not search for cocktail and wine prices directly. I estimated them from the local price relationship to beer and from typical rum-punch and wine-by-the-glass prices in the Caribbean, so they are less certain. The accommodation figures come from my general knowledge only, not from any booking pages or listings. Barbados has very few registered hostels, so the dorm and private-room figures in particular are uncertain. July is the low season, which may push room rates a little lower.
comparable_city_reasoning: I compared Bridgetown with other higher-cost Eastern Caribbean tourist capitals, such as Castries in St Lucia and St John's in Antigua. Restaurant and drink prices there are close to US levels, and hotel rates are well above the Latin American regional average.
